the autonomic nervous system can be used to infer the user's psychological state and that the accuracy of the inference can be improved by fusing the data from different physiological channels.

the most important prerequisites for data fusion and subsequent system adaptation are the choice of the psychological model, the preparation of the training set, the normalization of the features, the dimension reduction of the features and the choice of a classifier or an estimator.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in order to obtain a reliable classification of psychological states from autonomic nervous activity, it is necessary to: (1) select the appropriate psychological model, (2) use a sufficient training set, (3) extract a sufficient number of features, (4) normalize the features, (5) apply a dimension reduction method and (6) use a reliable classifier.
, in physiological computing, there are still many challenges to be overcome, but we have already made great progress in the past decade.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the best approach for a specific application depends on the type of physiological data available, the number of users and the number of states.
the most effective method of data fusion is a hybrid approach that uses both classification and regression techniques, as well as multiple features extracted from the data.
there is a large variety of methods that can be used in physiological computing.
